A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpinBench. Their main text, tables, figures, and appendices are sufficiently readable and matchable for reliable comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent identifying the substantive changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM evaluations, consistency and CoT analyses, and a twelve-participant human study in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds model evaluations, input-condition experiments, and GRPO fine-tuning and transfer results.

M1.justification: SpinBench retains its diagnostic framework, task-generation recipes, augmentation procedures, and scoring definitions. The additions extend benchmark coverage and evaluate existing models and training algorithms; they do not revise a proposed model architecture or introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix A adds mental rotation for cars and target objects in cluttered Infinigen scenes, extending the previous ABO-only coverage by 20 and 120 questions, respectively. Section 4.2 adds depth-augmented input scenarios, while Appendix E introduces transfer from object/face training tasks to Infinigen perspective taking.

E2.justification: Figure 3 adds GPT-5, o4-mini, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Qwen3-VL-4B, 8B, and 30B-A3B. Table 3 also adds Gemini to the reference-frame comparison. InternLM-XComposer2.5-7B disappears from the consistency-pattern comparison in v2 Figure 35, although its Table 5 entry remains.

E3.justification: New protocols compare standard images against horizontally concatenated depth maps and original-resolution inputs. Appendix E introduces six-epoch GRPO training on 5,900 examples, validation on a different task and domain, and comparison of initial versus highest validation reward. The existing Appendix D inference protocol remains unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 6 tests sensitivity to depth cues and image resolution. Appendix E tests whether training foundational spatial skills transfers to perspective taking and examines training versus validation behavior. Figure 40 adds the full OmniSpatial subtask-correlation matrix; the other three correlation matrices largely redisplay v1 Figure 36.

E5.justification: Figure 44 introduces shaded bands around learning curves, but neither its caption nor Appendix E defines their statistical meaning or reports independent run counts. Thus, a change in uncertainty estimation cannot be established reliably. Existing human-study standard deviations, correlation tests, and across-model error-bar practices are retained.

E6.justification: Matched existing Figure 3 cells remain unchanged, but new models and mental-rotation tasks substantially expand the results. GPT-5 and Gemini lead the expanded evaluation at 78.5% and 75.2% accuracy. New input experiments report generally worse depth-input performance and no systematic resolution benefit. Table 9 reports initial-to-best validation rewards of 0.344→0.389 and 0.302→0.398. Revised aggregate scores should not be interpreted as same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions of accuracy, consistency, and perfect rate are retained. Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees or proofs, and the added GRPO experiment introduces no mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims remain a cognitively grounded diagnostic benchmark, systematic spatial-reasoning weaknesses, task-dependent scaling, and alignment with human difficulty. Updating the abstract's evaluated-model count from 37 to 43 expands supporting evidence without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies the accuracy–consistency relationship among strong models and identifies GPT-5 as an exception to widespread reference-frame failures. It adds tentative explanations involving RGB training distributions and visual-encoder downsampling, qualifications about textual CoT, and interpretations of transfer and possible 4B overfitting in Appendix E.

D1.justification: v2 discloses the standard maximum image size of 256 and explains DepthAnything-based depth concatenation. Appendix E adds rollout and validation sampling settings, batch size, optimizer, learning rate, weight decay, and gradient clipping. Existing inference implementation details and the promise of a future code release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Theory of Space, Gemini 2.5, Qwen3, Depth Anything, and Machine Mental Imagery, while removing OST-Bench and SRBench discussion. MulSeT remains despite consolidation of its duplicate reference. The principal positioning around cognitive grounding and controlled diagnostic variation is retained.

P1.justification: The revision makes targeted prose edits, expands several results interpretations, spells out perspective-taking subtype headings, and adds Appendix E on fine-tuning. Conference headers and acknowledgments also appear. Most existing exposition and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Main and appendix heatmaps expand with model rows and mental-rotation columns, and ranking and consistency graphics are updated. New displays include the input-condition comparison, learning curves, and Table 9. The combined correlation heatmap becomes four separate figures, and Table 5 now spans two pages. These are substantive display changes beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The input controls and transfer experiment provide a modest net gain by testing explanations and compositional generalization left untested in v1. Their value is limited by peak-validation selection, undefined learning-curve bands, and new reporting inconsistencies: Table 5 duplicates Qwen2.5-VL-32B with conflicting accuracies, while Figure 4's caption retains r=0.874 despite the revised plot reporting r=0.891.
